The *Naḷāgārikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 347) is a biographical narrative poem located within the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The poem records the past deeds and spiritual attainment of the elder (*thera*) Naḷāgārika [SuttaCentral]. While no specialized modern studies are represented in the catalogued reference passages, SuttaCentral registers five translations of the text into five languages [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analyses generated by DharmaNexus show that the *Naḷāgārikattheraapadāna* shares 55 passages with eight other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive reuse occurs in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (both parts 1 and 2), which cite or parallel substantial portions of the text (such as §0.3–2.4 corresponding to §3143_9–3147) [DharmaNexus]. The text also exhibits extensive internal formulaic reuse with other poems in the *Therāpadāna*, sharing an identical opening section (§0.3–2.4) with the *Naḷakuṭidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 501), alongside overlapping verses in the *Tikaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 503), *Ekadussadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 336), *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 425), *Ukkhittapadumiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 342), and *Sucintitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 430) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns segments of the text with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (especially §2.1–2.4) and a Tibetan text, though SuttaCentral does not record any curated cross-canonical parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
